svg.text: Which DGX Spark cluster runs which models (decode speeds from published benchmarks)
Decode tok/s ~ 273 GB/s / active weights in GB - MoE models with small active params are the whole ballgame
TIER 1 - One DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified, 273 GB/s, 1 PFLOP FP4)
gpt-oss-20b MXFP4: 83-86 tok/s. gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 (59 GiB): 55-60 tok/s. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B NVFP4: 51-72 tok/s.
Qwen3.8-27B dense: 34 tok/s. Dense is the wall: 32B Q4 ~11 tok/s, Llama 3.1 70B FP8 just 2.7 tok/s decode.
~120 GB visible to the GPU. Prompt processing is elite: 1,725-10,257 tok/s across model classes (NVIDIA, llama.cpp, LMSYS).
Shipped Oct 2025 at $3,999; Founders Edition now $4,699, partner boxes roughly $5,999-$6,999 in late 2026.
TIER 2 - Two Sparks over ConnectX-7 200 GbE RDMA (~240 GB pool) - THE VALIDATED SWEET SPOT
Qwen3-235B-A22B FP4: 11.7 tok/s (NVIDIA, TensorRT-LLM). DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark: ~60-67 tok/s at up to 1M context.
GLM-5.3 Flash: ~22 tok/s (community). Class of 405B FP4 reachable. Prefill up to 23,477 tok/s on 235B FP4.
Pipeline parallelism beats tensor parallelism for batched work: 554.7 vs 252.0 tok/s on gpt-oss-120b at batch 128 (StorageReview).
TIER 3 - Four Sparks (~480 GB pooled, NVIDIA-validated up to 700B parameters)
Llama 3.3 70B tensor-parallel: ~4x speedup vs one box. Batched throughput scales ~18,400 to ~74,600 tok/s from 1 to 4 nodes.
Sharing a model that already fits one box costs speed: 35B-A3B at TP=2 gives 99 tok/s, TP=4 drops to 89.
NVIDIA sells a validated four-unit configuration; ring or switch topologies both documented in playbooks.
TIER 4 - Six to eight Sparks (community racks on 200G RoCE fabric)
GLM-5.2 753B: 7.4 tok/s on 6 nodes (TP=2 x PP=3). Mimo 2.6 1020B-A42B: 68.3 tok/s on 8 Sparks with speculative decoding.
Concurrency is where clusters shine: 128 simultaneous streams sustained 1,403 tok/s aggregate on 35B-A3B across 2 nodes.
6-node build details: MikroTik CRS804 switch, ~196 Gbps per link, ~104 GB GPU-visible budget per node after OS overhead.
Sources: NVIDIA product page + Technical Blog (Oct 2025, Mar 2026), StorageReview, llamaperf, Level1Techs, NVIDIA Developer Forums - speeds vary with engine, quant and context.
